chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: “The sick person must give the adhān and iqāmah when he intends salat (prayer), even if only within himself, if he is unable to speak it verbally.”
He was asked: “What if he is in severe pain?” He said: “He must still give the adhān and iqāmah, for there is no salat (prayer) except with adhān and iqāmah.”

key_terms.إِقَامَةٍ: the second call immediately preceding salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْمَرِيضِ: the sick person who is the subject of this ruling
key_terms.فِي نَفْسِهِ: inwardly, within oneself, without vocal expression
key_terms.يُؤَذِّنَ: to recite the adhān before salat (prayer)
key_terms.يُقِيمَ: to recite the iqāmah before beginning salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: Does a sick person still need to say the adhān and iqāmah before salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith states that a sick person should not leave the adhān and iqāmah when preparing for salat (prayer), even if he can only recite them inwardly due to inability to speak. It emphasizes the importance of adhān and iqāmah in the performance of prayer, even under hardship and severe pain.
